questions.q: For which values of k does x² + kx + 9 = 0 have equal roots?
questions.why: Equal roots need b² − 4ac = 0: k² − 36 = 0, so k = ±6.

questions.q: Write x² − 6x + 11 in completed-square form.
questions.why: x² − 6x = (x − 3)² − 9, so the expression is (x − 3)² + 2; the minimum point is (3, 2).

questions.q: Solve x² − 5x + 4 < 0.
questions.why: (x − 1)(x − 4) < 0 between the roots.

questions.q: The equation 2x² + 3x + k = 0 has no real roots. Which describes the possible values of k?
questions.why: No real roots needs b² − 4ac < 0: 9 − 8k < 0, so k > 9/8.

questions.q: Solve x − 5√x + 6 = 0.
questions.why: Let u = √x: u² − 5u + 6 = 0 gives u = 2 or 3, so x = u² = 4 or 9.

long.q: Express 2x² − 12x + 23 in the form a(x + b)² + c. Hence state the coordinates of the minimum point of y = 2x² − 12x + 23.
The line y = kx − 1 is a tangent to the curve y = x² + 3. Find the possible values of k.
scheme: M1: equate and rearrange: x² − kx + 4 = 0

long.q: Find the set of values of the constant k for which the equation kx² + 4x + (k − 3) = 0 has two distinct real roots.
scheme: M1: critical values from (k − 4)(k + 1): k = −1 and k = 4

long.q: By using a suitable substitution, solve the equation 2x − 7√x + 3 = 0.
The line y = 2x + 1 meets the curve y = x² − 3x + 5 at the points A and B. Find the coordinates of A and B, and the exact length of AB.

questions.q: f(x) = 2x + 3. What is f⁻¹(x)?
questions.why: Swap and rearrange: x = 2y + 3, so y = (x − 3)/2.

questions.q: f(x) = x² and g(x) = x + 1. What is fg(x)?
A function has an inverse only if it is…
questions.why: Each output must come from exactly one input.

questions.q: f(x) = x² + 1 for x ≥ 0. Which is the range of f?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): there was confusion between range and domain. The domain is x ≥ 0; the range is the set of outputs f(x) ≥ 1.

questions.q: The graph of y = f(x) is stretched by factor 2 parallel to the y-axis, then translated 3 units in the negative x-direction. What is the equation of the new graph?
questions.why: A y-stretch of factor 2 multiplies the output: 2f(x). Moving 3 units left replaces x by x + 3, giving y = 2f(x + 3).

long.q: f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x² + 1. Find fg(x) and solve fg(x) = 10.
f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x − 3) for x ≠ 3. Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).

The graph of y = f(x) is transformed to the graph of y = 3f(x − 2). (a) Describe fully the two transformations. (b) The point (1, 4) lies on y = f(x). State the coordinates of the corresponding point on y = 3f(x − 2).
scheme: B1: by 2 units in the positive x-direction, vector (2, 0)
B1: a stretch parallel to the y-axis
long.ans: translation (2, 0); stretch parallel to y-axis, factor 3; (3, 12)

long.q: The function f is defined by f(x) = (x − 3)² + 1 for x ≥ k. (a) State the smallest value of k for which f has an inverse. (b) For this value of k, find an expression for f⁻¹(x) and state the domain of f⁻¹.
scheme: B1: k = 3 (the vertex of the parabola)

long.q: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = 2x − 1 for x ∈ ℝ and g(x) = x² − 4x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 5. (a) Find the range of g. (b) Solve the equation gf(x) = 0.
scheme: B1: g(x) = (x − 2)² − 4, so the least value is −4 at x = 2
M1: consider the end of the domain: g(5) = 5

questions.q: What is the centre and radius of (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25?
questions.why: (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r² has centre (a, b) and radius r.

questions.q: What is the length of the line from (1, 2) to (4, 6)?
What is the gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8)?
A line passes through (2, 5) and is perpendicular to y = 3x − 1. What is its equation?
questions.why: The perpendicular gradient is −1/3, so y − 5 = −⅓(x − 2), which rearranges to x + 3y = 17.

questions.q: The line y = 2x + c is a tangent to the circle x² + y² = 5. What are the possible values of c?
questions.why: Substituting gives 5x² + 4cx + c² − 5 = 0; a tangent needs a repeated root, so 16c² − 20(c² − 5) = 0, giving c² = 25 and c = ±5.

long.q: A is the point (1, 2) and B is the point (7, 10). Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB.
scheme: M1: perpendicular gradient −3/4 through the midpoint

long.q: A circle has equation x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0. Find its centre and radius.

A circle has equation (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25, and P(5, 3) lies on the circle. Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at P, and the coordinates of the point where this tangent meets the x-axis.
scheme: M1: gradient of the radius from (2, −1) to (5, 3) is 4/3

long.q: Find the values of the constant k for which the line y = 2x + k is a tangent to the circle x² + y² = 20.
scheme: M1: substitute y = 2x + k into the circle

long.q: The points A, B and C have coordinates (−1, 3), (3, 5) and (5, 1). (a) Show that angle ABC is a right angle. (b) Find the area of triangle ABC. (c) Find the equation of the circle that passes through A, B and C.
scheme: M1: find the gradients of AB and BC
A1: 1/2 and −2, product −1, so AB is perpendicular to BC
M1: AC is a diameter (angle in a semicircle), so the centre is the midpoint of AC, (2, 2)

questions.q: An arc of a circle of radius 6 cm subtends 0.5 radians. How long is the arc?
The area of a sector of radius 4 and angle 1.2 rad is…
A sector has radius 5 cm and angle 0.8 radians. What is its perimeter?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some found an area instead of a perimeter. Arc = 5 × 0.8 = 4, plus two radii.

questions.q: A sector of a circle of radius 4 cm has area 12 cm². What is the angle of the sector?
questions.why: Area = ½r²θ, so 12 = ½ × 16 × θ and θ = 1.5 rad. Forgetting the ½ gives 0.75.

questions.q: A chord AB of a circle of radius 6 cm subtends an angle of π/3 at the centre. What is the exact area of the minor segment cut off by AB?
questions.why: Sector = ½ × 36 × π/3 = 6π and triangle = ½ × 36 × sin(π/3) = 9√3, so the segment is 6π − 9√3 cm².

long.q: The diagram shows a sector OAB of a circle with centre O and radius 8 cm. Angle AOB = 1.2 radians. Find (a) the length of the arc AB, (b) the area of the segment between the arc AB and the chord AB.
Convert 135° to radians, giving your answer in terms of π. Find the area of a sector of radius 6 cm with this angle.
A sector of a circle has radius r cm and angle θ radians. Its perimeter is 20 cm and its area is 16 cm². Find the values of r and θ.
scheme: M1: eliminate θ to obtain r² − 10r + 16 = 0
A1: r = 8 (r = 2 rejected because it gives θ = 8, more than 2π)

long.q: A circle has centre O and radius 10 cm. A chord AB has length 12 cm. Find angle AOB in radians, and the perimeter of the minor segment cut off by AB.
scheme: M1: sin(½ AOB) = 6/10 (or use the cosine rule)

long.q: OAB is a sector of a circle with centre O, radius 6 cm and angle AOB = π/3 radians. The tangent to the arc at A meets OB produced at C. Find the exact area of the region bounded by AC, CB and the arc AB.
scheme: B1: OA is perpendicular to AC, so AC = 6 tan(π/3) = 6√3
M1: area of triangle OAC = ½ × 6 × 6√3

questions.q: Which identity is always true?
o: tan θ = cos θ / sin θ
questions.why: This is the fundamental Pythagorean identity.

questions.q: Solve sin x = 0.5 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
questions.why: Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants: 30° and 180° − 30°.

questions.q: What is the period of y = cos 2x?
questions.why: The period of cos kx is 360°/k.

questions.q: Solve sin θ = 0.6 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°. How many solutions are there?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): candidates often gave too few answers. Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants: 36.9° and 143.1°.

questions.q: What is the derivative of y = (3x − 2)⁴ with respect to x?
questions.why: By the chain rule, dy/dx = 4(3x − 2)³ × d/dx(3x − 2) = 4(3x − 2)³ × 3 = 12(3x − 2)³.

long.q: Solve the equation 2 sin²θ + 3 cos θ = 3 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
scheme: M1: solve the quadratic in cos θ

long.q: Prove the identity (1 − cos²x)/(1 − sin²x) ≡ tan²x.
scheme: M1: 1 − cos²x = sin²x and 1 − sin²x = cos²x

long.q: Solve the equation 3 sin θ tan θ = 8 for 0° < θ < 360°.
scheme: M1: use tan θ = sin θ / cos θ to get 3 sin²θ = 8 cos θ

long.q: The function f is defined by f(x) = a + b cos x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, where a and b are constants. Given that f(0) = 7 and f(π) = −1, find a and b, and solve f(x) = 0.
scheme: M1: a + b = 7 and a − b = −1

long.q: Prove the identity 1/cos θ − cos θ ≡ sin θ tan θ. Hence solve 1/cos θ − cos θ = 2 sin θ for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
scheme: A1: sin²θ / cos θ = sin θ tan θ, shown convincingly
M1: sin θ (tan θ − 2) = 0, without dividing by sin θ

questions.q: What is the coefficient of x² in (1 + 2x)⁵?
A geometric series has a = 8 and r = ½. What is its sum to infinity?
questions.why: S∞ = a/(1 − r) = 8 ÷ ½ = 16, valid because |r| < 1.

questions.q: The 10th term of the arithmetic progression 3, 7, 11, … is…
In the expansion of (3 + ax)⁴, what is the coefficient of x²?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): the coefficient was often given as 54a rather than 54a². 4C2 × 3² × a² = 6 × 9 × a².

questions.q: Evaluate the definite integral ∫₀² (3x² + 2x) dx.

long.q: Find the coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (2 − x)⁶.
The first term of a geometric progression is 81 and its sum to infinity is 243. Find the common ratio and the fourth term.

The third term of an arithmetic progression is 11 and the sum of the first 10 terms is 185. Find the first term and the common difference, and the least number of terms for which the sum exceeds 1000.
(a) Find the first three terms, in ascending powers of x, in the expansion of (1 − x/2)⁸. (b) Hence find the coefficient of x² in the expansion of (3 + 2x)(1 − x/2)⁸.
scheme: M1: two products give x²: 3 × 7 and 2 × (−4)

long.q: An arithmetic progression has first term 4 and common difference d, where d ≠ 0. The first, fifth and twenty-first terms of this progression are, in that order, the first three terms of a geometric progression. Find d and the common ratio of the geometric progression.
scheme: M1: fifth term 4 + 4d and twenty-first term 4 + 20d

questions.q: Differentiate y = 3x⁴ − 2x.
questions.why: d/dx(axⁿ) = naxⁿ⁻¹.

questions.q: At a stationary point, dy/dx equals…
questions.why: The gradient is zero; the second derivative tells maximum or minimum.

questions.q: Differentiate y = (2x + 1)³.
questions.why: Chain rule: 3(2x + 1)² × 2.

questions.q: The radius of a circle increases at 0.5 cm s⁻¹. At what rate is the area increasing when the radius is 4 cm?
questions.why: dA/dt = dA/dr × dr/dt = 2πr × 0.5 = 2π × 4 × 0.5 = 4π cm² s⁻¹.

questions.q: What is the gradient of the curve y = 2√x at the point where x = 4?
questions.why: y = 2x^(1/2), so dy/dx = x^(−1/2) = 1/√x, which is 1/2 at x = 4.

long.q: A curve has equation y = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 2. Find the coordinates of the stationary points and determine their nature.
scheme: A1: (1, 6) is a maximum, (3, 2) a minimum

long.q: Find the equation of the normal to the curve y = 4/x at the point (2, 2).

A curve has equation y = √(4x + 1). A point moves along the curve so that its x-coordinate increases at a rate of 0.3 units per second. Find the rate at which the y-coordinate is increasing when x = 2.
scheme: M1: dy/dt = dy/dx × dx/dt, with dy/dx = 2/3 at x = 2

long.q: f(x) = 2x³ + 3x² − 12x + 5. Find the set of values of x for which f is a decreasing function.
scheme: M1: solve f′(x) < 0, critical values from 6(x + 2)(x − 1)

long.q: A closed cylindrical can has radius r cm, height h cm and volume 250π cm³. (a) Show that its total surface area, A cm², is given by A = 2πr² + 500π/r. (b) Find the value of r for which A is stationary, find this value of A, and determine its nature.

questions.q: Find ∫ 6x² dx.
questions.why: Raise the power by one and divide: 6x³/3 = 2x³.

questions.q: Evaluate ∫₀² 3x² dx.
questions.why: [x³]₀² = 8.

questions.q: The region under y = f(x) is rotated 360° about the x-axis. The volume is:
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some integrated y rather than y².

questions.q: Find ∫ (3x + 2)⁴ dx.
questions.why: Raise the power by 1 and divide by the new power and by the coefficient of x: (3x + 2)⁵/(5 × 3) + c.

questions.q: The region under y = √x from x = 0 to x = 4 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. What is the volume generated?
questions.why: V = π∫₀⁴ y² dx = π∫₀⁴ x dx = π[x²/2]₀⁴ = 8π. Using ∫y dx instead of ∫y² dx gives 16π/3.

long.q: The diagram shows the curve y = x² − 4x + 3, which crosses the x-axis at x = 1 and x = 3. Find the area of the shaded region between the curve and the x-axis.
A curve has gradient dy/dx = 6x² − 2x and passes through the point (1, 5). Find the equation of the curve.
Find the exact value of ∫₁⁵ 6/√(2x − 1) dx.
scheme: M1: integral of the form k(2x − 1)^(½)

long.q: The region bounded by the curve y = 3/x, the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = 3 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed.
scheme: M1: V = π ∫ y² dx with y² = 9/x²

long.q: The curve y = 6x − x² and the line y = 2x meet at two points. Find the x-coordinates of these points and the area of the region enclosed between the curve and the line.
scheme: M1: area = ∫ (curve − line) dx from 0 to 4 (or curve area − triangle)

questions.q: Solve |x − 3| < 2.
What is the remainder when x³ − 2x + 1 is divided by (x − 2)?
questions.why: Remainder theorem: f(2) = 8 − 4 + 1 = 5.

questions.q: Solve |2x − 3| < 5.
Express (5x + 1)/((x − 1)(x + 2)) in partial fractions.
questions.why: 5x + 1 = A(x + 2) + B(x − 1). x = 1 gives 6 = 3A so A = 2; x = −2 gives −9 = −3B so B = 3.

questions.q: What is the expansion of (1 − 3x)⁻¹ up to the term in x², and for which x is it valid?
questions.why: (1 + u)⁻¹ = 1 − u + u² with u = −3x gives 1 + 3x + 9x²; it is valid when |3x| < 1, i.e. |x| < 1/3.

long.q: Expand (1 + 2x)^(−1/2) in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x², and state the set of values of x for which the expansion is valid.
Solve the inequality |2x − 3| < |x + 1|.
scheme: M1: square both sides (or solve the two linear equations 2x − 3 = ±(x + 1))
A1: critical values x = 2/3 and x = 4

long.q: The polynomial p(x) = 2x³ + ax² + bx − 6, where a and b are constants. (x − 2) is a factor of p(x), and when p(x) is divided by (x + 1) the remainder is −6. (a) Find a and b. (b) Show that the equation p(x) = 0 has only one real root.
scheme: A1: its discriminant 9 − 24 < 0, so x = 2 is the only real root

long.q: Express (x + 5)/((1 − x)(2 + x)) in partial fractions. Hence obtain its expansion in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x².
scheme: M1: (2 + x)⁻¹ = ½(1 + ½x)⁻¹ = ½(1 − ½x + ¼x²)

long.q: Find the quotient and the remainder when x⁴ + 3x² − 2x + 1 is divided by x² − x + 2.
scheme: M1: long division reaching a quotient of the form x² + px + q

questions.q: Solve eˣ = 5.
questions.why: Take natural logs of both sides.

questions.q: log 8 + log 2 equals…
questions.why: log a + log b = log(ab) = log 16.

questions.q: Solve 3ˣ = 20, giving x to 3 significant figures.
questions.why: x = ln 20 ÷ ln 3. Examiners (2023): keep brackets when taking logarithms.

questions.q: Solve ln(x + 2) = 1 + ln x.
questions.why: ln((x + 2)/x) = 1, so x + 2 = ex, giving x(e − 1) = 2 and x = 2/(e − 1).

questions.q: Variables satisfy y = Axⁿ. A graph of ln y against ln x is a straight line with gradient 1.5 and intercept 0.7 on the ln y axis. What are n and A?
questions.why: ln y = ln A + n ln x, so the gradient is n = 1.5 and the intercept is ln A = 0.7, giving A = e^0.7 ≈ 2.01.

long.q: Solve the equation 3^(2x) − 5(3^x) + 4 = 0, giving any non-integer answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Two variables x and y satisfy y = A × bˣ, where A and b are constants. The graph of ln y against x is a straight line passing through the points (1, 2.0) and (4, 3.5). Find A and b, correct to 3 significant figures.
scheme: B1: ln y = ln A + x ln b

long.q: Solve the equation ln(2x + 3) = 2 ln x + ln 5.
scheme: M1: combine logs correctly: ln(2x + 3) = ln(5x²)
B1: x = −3/5 rejected, since ln x is undefined for x < 0

long.q: Solve the inequality 2^(x + 1) > 5ˣ, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
scheme: M1: take logarithms: (x + 1) ln 2 > x ln 5
M1: collect x terms: x(ln 5 − ln 2) < ln 2

long.q: The mass, m grams, of a radioactive sample after t days is given by m = 50e^(−kt), where k is a constant. After 10 days the mass is 35 grams. Find k, and the time taken for the mass to fall to 10 grams.

questions.q: cos 2A can be written as…
questions.why: cos 2A = cos²A − sin²A = 1 − 2sin²A = 2cos²A − 1.

questions.q: sec θ is…
questions.why: sec = 1/cos, cosec = 1/sin, cot = 1/tan.

questions.q: sec²θ − tan²θ is equal to:
questions.why: From 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ.

questions.q: Given that tan A = 3/4 and A is acute, what is tan 2A?
What is the exact value of sin 75°?

long.q: Express 3 sin θ + 4 cos θ in the form R sin(θ + α), where R > 0 and 0° < α < 90°. Hence solve 3 sin θ + 4 cos θ = 2 for 0° < θ < 360°.
Solve the equation cos 2θ + 3 sin θ = 2 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
Solve the equation 2cot²x + 3 cosec x = 0 for 0° < x < 360°.
scheme: M1: solve the quadratic in cosec x
A1: cosec x = −2 (cosec x = ½ is impossible)

long.q: Prove the identity sin 2θ / (1 + cos 2θ) ≡ tan θ. Hence solve the equation sin 4θ / (1 + cos 4θ) = 3 for 0° < θ < 180°.
scheme: M1: sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ
A1: 2 sin θ cos θ / 2cos²θ = tan θ, shown

long.q: Given that sin(x + 30°) = 2 cos(x − 60°), find the exact value of tan x, and solve the equation for 0° < x < 360°.
scheme: M1: expand both sides with the compound-angle formulae
A1: (√3/2) sin x + ½ cos x = cos x + √3 sin x

questions.q: Differentiate y = x eˣ.
questions.why: Product rule: eˣ + x eˣ.

questions.q: Differentiate y = ln(3x).
questions.why: ln(3x) = ln 3 + ln x, so the derivative is 1/x.

questions.q: y = x² e^(2x). Which method is needed to find dy/dx?
o: Product rule (with the chain rule for e^(2x))
questions.why: Examiners (2023): it was essential that y be differentiated as a product; many did not recognise it as one.

questions.q: Differentiate y = (ln x)/x.
questions.why: Quotient rule: (x × 1/x − ln x × 1)/x² = (1 − ln x)/x².

questions.q: A curve has equation x² + y² = 25. What is dy/dx at the point (3, 4)?
questions.why: Differentiating implicitly: 2x + 2y dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = −x/y = −3/4.

long.q: Find dy/dx when y = x² e^(3x), and the exact x-coordinates of the stationary points.
The curve y = (ln x)/x² has one stationary point. Find its exact coordinates.
scheme: M1: set dy/dx = 0, so ln x = ½

long.q: A curve has parametric equations x = 3t², y = 2t³ − 6t. Find dy/dx in terms of t, and the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where t = 2.
A curve has equation x² + 3xy + y² = 11. Find dy/dx in terms of x and y, and the equation of the normal to the curve at the point (1, 2).
scheme: B1: 2x and 2y dy/dx from the squared terms

long.q: Find the x-coordinate of the stationary point of the curve y = e^(2x) cos x for 0 < x < π/2, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
scheme: A1: dy/dx = 2e^(2x) cos x − e^(2x) sin x
M1: set dy/dx = 0, so tan x = 2

questions.q: Find ∫ 1/x dx (x > 0).
questions.why: The derivative of ln x is 1/x.

questions.q: Which method suits ∫ x cos x dx?
questions.why: u = x, dv = cos x dx gives x sin x + cos x + c.
Divide by the derivative of the inside, 2.

questions.q: Evaluate ∫₀^(π/2) sin²x dx.
questions.why: sin²x = ½(1 − cos 2x), so the integral is [x/2 − (sin 2x)/4] from 0 to π/2 = π/4.

questions.q: Find ∫ 2x/(x² + 1) dx.
questions.why: The numerator 2x is exactly the derivative of the denominator, so the integral is ln(x² + 1) + c.

long.q: Use integration by parts to find ∫ x ln x dx.
scheme: M1: u = ln x, dv/dx = x

long.q: Use the substitution u = x + 1 to find the exact value of ∫₀³ x/√(x + 1) dx.
scheme: B1: du = dx and new limits 1 and 4

long.q: Express 4/(x² − 1) in partial fractions, and hence find the exact value of ∫₂⁴ 4/(x² − 1) dx, giving your answer as a single logarithm.
By using a double-angle formula, find the exact value of ∫₀^(π/4) 4 sin²x dx.
Use the trapezium rule with two intervals to estimate ∫₀² √(1 + x³) dx, giving your answer correct to 2 decimal places. State, with a reason, whether this is an over-estimate or an under-estimate.
scheme: B1: over-estimate, because the curve is convex (bends upwards), so each chord lies above the curve

questions.q: f(1) = −2 and f(2) = 3, with f continuous. What can you conclude?
questions.why: A change of sign shows a root in the interval.

questions.q: An iteration converges to 0.79495… What is the root correct to 2 decimal places?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): a common error was rounding the final answer to 0.80 rather than 0.79.

questions.q: A sign change of f(x) between a and b shows a root only if f is:
questions.why: A function like 1/x changes sign at an asymptote, with no root.

questions.q: The iteration xₙ₊₁ = ½(xₙ + 5/xₙ) converges to a value α. Which equation does α satisfy?
questions.why: At the limit x = ½(x + 5/x), so 2x = x + 5/x, giving x = 5/x and x² = 5.

questions.q: Using xₙ₊₁ = ∛(xₙ + 3) with x₁ = 2, what is x₂ to 3 decimal places?
questions.why: x₂ = ∛(2 + 3) = ∛5 = 1.70997…, which is 1.710 to 3 decimal places.

long.q: (a) Show by calculation that the equation ln x + x − 3 = 0 has a root between x = 2 and x = 3. (b) Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = 3 − ln xₙ, with x₁ = 2, to find this root correct to 2 decimal places. Give each iterate to 4 decimal places.
scheme: M1: evaluate f(x) = ln x + x − 3 at x = 2 and x = 3
A1: f(2) = −0.307 and f(3) = 1.099; sign change, so a root lies between
M1: use the iteration correctly at least once (2.3069)
A1: root 2.21, after enough iterates to show it to 2 d.p.

long.q: By sketching the graphs of y = e^(−x) and y = x on the same axes, state the number of real roots of the equation e^(−x) = x. Verify by calculation that the root lies between 0.5 and 0.6.
scheme: B1: sketch: decreasing exponential through (0, 1), and the line y = x through the origin
B1: they cross once, so there is exactly one real root
M1: evaluate e^(−x) − x at x = 0.5 and x = 0.6
A1: 0.107 and −0.051; sign change, so the root lies between 0.5 and 0.6

long.q: A chord AB of a circle with centre O subtends an angle of x radians at O. The area of the minor segment cut off by AB is one third of the area of triangle OAB. (a) Show that x = (4/3) sin x. (b) Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = (4/3) sin xₙ, with x₁ = 1.3, to find x correct to 3 decimal places. Give each iterate to 4 decimal places.
scheme: B1: segment area = ½r²(x − sin x)
M1: ½r²(x − sin x) = ⅓ × ½r² sin x
M1: use the iteration correctly at least once (1.2847)

long.q: (a) Show by calculation that the equation cot x = x, with x in radians, has a root between 0.8 and 0.9. (b) Show that this root satisfies x = tan⁻¹(1/x). (c) Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = tan⁻¹(1/xₙ), with x₁ = 0.85, to find the root correct to 2 decimal places. Give each iterate to 4 decimal places.
scheme: M1: evaluate cot x − x at x = 0.8 and x = 0.9
A1: 0.171 and −0.106; sign change, so a root lies between
B1: cot x = x gives tan x = 1/x, so x = tan⁻¹(1/x)
M1: use the iteration correctly at least once (0.8663)

long.q: The sequence given by xₙ₊₁ = 2xₙ/3 + 4/(3xₙ²), with x₁ = 2, converges to α. (a) Find α correct to 3 decimal places, giving each iterate to 5 decimal places. (b) State an equation satisfied by α and hence find the exact value of α.
scheme: M1: use the iteration correctly at least once (1.66667)

questions.q: What is the scalar product of (1, 2, 3) and (4, −1, 0)?
Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular when their scalar product is…
a = (1, 2, 2) and b = (2, −1, 0). What is the angle between them?
questions.why: a · b = 2 − 2 + 0 = 0, so they are perpendicular.

P lies on the line r = (2, 1, 0) + t(1, −1, 2). For which value of t is OP perpendicular to the line?

long.q: The lines l₁: r = (1, 2, 3) + s(1, 0, −1) and l₂: r = (2, 1, 0) + t(0, 1, 1). Show that they do not intersect.
scheme: M1: equate components: 1 + s = 2, 2 = 1 + t, 3 − s = t
A1: third equation: 3 − 1 = 2 ≠ 1, so no intersection (and not parallel, so skew)

long.q: Relative to the origin O, the points A and B have position vectors 2i + j − 2k and 3i + 4k. Find angle AOB.

The lines l and m have equations r = (i + j) + s(2i + j − k) and r = (5i + 3k) + t(i − j + 2k). Show that the lines intersect, find the position vector of the point of intersection, and find the acute angle between the lines.
scheme: A1: s = 1, t = −2 from two equations
A1: third equation checked: −1 = 3 − 4, so the lines intersect
M1: scalar product of the directions: 2 − 1 − 2 = −1, with both moduli √6

long.q: The line l has equation r = (i + 2k) + λ(i + 2j + 2k), and the point P has position vector 4i + j + 4k. Find the position vector of the foot N of the perpendicular from P to l, and the perpendicular distance from P to l.
scheme: M1: general point on l and PN = (λ − 3)i + (2λ − 1)j + (2λ − 2)k

long.q: OABC is a parallelogram, where O is the origin and A and B have position vectors 3i − j + 2k and 5i + 2j + 3k. (a) Find the position vector of C. (b) Find the unit vector in the direction of AC. (c) Find angle AOC.

questions.q: The general solution of dy/dx = ky is…
questions.why: Separate variables: ∫dy/y = ∫k dx, ln y = kx + c.

questions.q: What is the general solution of dy/dx = 2y?
questions.why: Separate: ∫ dy/y = ∫ 2 dx, ln y = 2x + c.

questions.q: Separating the variables in dy/dx = x/y gives:
questions.why: Examiners (2023): incorrect separation of variables was a common error.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = xy, given that y = 1 when x = 0.
questions.why: ∫ (1/y) dy = ∫ x dx gives ln y = x²/2 + c; y = 1 at x = 0 gives c = 0, so y = e^(x²/2).

questions.q: A population P decreases at a rate proportional to the square root of P. Which differential equation models this (k > 0)?
questions.why: The rate of change is dP/dt; it is proportional to √P and negative because P decreases.

long.q: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = xy² given that y = 1 when x = 0.
scheme: M1: separate: ∫ y⁻² dy = ∫ x dx

long.q: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = 2x e^(−y), given that y = 0 when x = 1. Give y in terms of x.
scheme: A1: y = 2 ln x (= ln x²)

long.q: Liquid leaks from a tank so that the rate at which the volume, V m³, decreases is proportional to √V. Initially V = 100, and after 10 minutes V = 64. Form and solve a differential equation to find V in terms of t, and find the time at which the tank becomes empty.
scheme: M1: separate and integrate: ∫ V^(−½) dV = −∫ k dt
M1: use both conditions: c = 20 and k = 0.4

long.q: The variable x satisfies dx/dt = x(4 − x), and x = 1 when t = 0. (a) Find the exact value of t when x = 2. (b) State what happens to x as t becomes large.
scheme: M1: partial fractions: 1/(x(4 − x)) = ¼(1/x + 1/(4 − x))
A1: ¼ ln x − ¼ ln(4 − x) = t + c
M1: use x = 1, t = 0: c = −¼ ln 3

long.q: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = y tan x for −π/2 < x < π/2, given that y = 2 when x = 0. Find the value of y when x = π/3.
scheme: M1: separate: ∫ (1/y) dy = ∫ tan x dx
A1: ln y = −ln(cos x) + c (= ln sec x + c)
M1: use y = 2 when x = 0 to find the constant

questions.q: What is (2 + 3i)(1 − i)?
What is the modulus of 3 − 4i?

questions.why: A number times its conjugate is the modulus squared: 4 + 9.

questions.q: Express (3 + i)/(1 − i) in the form x + iy.
questions.why: Multiply top and bottom by 1 + i: (3 + 3i + i + i²)/(1 + 1) = (2 + 4i)/2 = 1 + 2i.

questions.q: In an Argand diagram, what is the locus of z satisfying |z − 2i| = 3?
o: A circle with centre (0, −2) and radius 3
A circle with centre (0, 2) and radius 9
A circle with centre (0, 2) and radius 3
questions.why: |z − a| = r is a circle of radius r centred on the point a; here a = 2i, the point (0, 2), and r = 3.

long.q: The complex number z = 1 + i√3. Find the modulus and argument of z, and hence find z³.
scheme: M1: z³ has modulus 8, argument π

long.q: Find the two square roots of the complex number −3 + 4i, giving your answers in the form x + iy, where x and y are real.
scheme: M1: (x + iy)² = −3 + 4i, equate real and imaginary parts
M1: eliminate y to get x⁴ + 3x² − 4 = 0

long.q: On an Argand diagram, the locus of the complex number z satisfies |z − 3i| = |z + 1|. (a) Describe the locus geometrically. (b) Find its Cartesian equation. (c) Find the least value of |z| for points on the locus.
scheme: B1: the perpendicular bisector of the points representing 3i and −1
M1: substitute z = x + iy and square both moduli
M1: perpendicular distance from the origin to the line

long.q: Given that 1 + 2i is a root of the equation z³ + az² + bz − 15 = 0, where a and b are real, find a and b and the other two roots.
scheme: B1: 1 − 2i is also a root (real coefficients)
M1: third factor from the constant term: (z − 3)

long.q: The complex numbers u and v are u = 1 + i and v = √3 + i. (a) Find the modulus and argument of u and of v. (b) Hence find the modulus and argument of u/v. (c) By writing u/v in the form x + iy, find the exact value of tan(π/12).
scheme: M1: divide the moduli and subtract the arguments
M1: multiply by the conjugate: u/v = ((√3 + 1) + i(√3 − 1))/4

questions.q: Limiting friction is given by F = μR. What is R?
questions.why: R is the normal reaction; it equals the weight only on a horizontal surface with no other vertical forces.

questions.q: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces. Their resultant is…
questions.why: Equilibrium means no resultant force: the forces form a closed triangle.

questions.q: A 4 kg block rests on a rough horizontal plane with μ = 0.5 (g = 10 m s⁻²). The greatest friction possible is…
questions.why: R = 4 × 10 = 40 N, and limiting friction is μR = 0.5 × 40 = 20 N.

questions.q: A particle of weight mg rests on a slope at angle θ to the horizontal. The component of its weight down the slope is…
questions.why: Resolve parallel to the slope: mg sin θ; perpendicular to it: mg cos θ.

questions.q: A force of 10 N acts at 30° to the horizontal. What is its horizontal component?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): candidates confused sin and cos when resolving; the component adjacent to the angle uses cos.

long.q: A particle of mass 2 kg rests on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. A force of P N acts on it up the plane, parallel to a line of greatest slope. The coefficient of friction is 0.4. Find the least value of P for which the particle does not slide down the plane. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: M1: resolve along the plane with friction acting up the plane

long.q: A particle of mass 3 kg hangs in equilibrium, supported by two light strings attached to fixed points. One string makes an angle of 30° with the vertical and the other makes an angle of 60° with the vertical, on the opposite side. Find the tension in each string. (g = 10 m s⁻²)

A box of mass 8 kg rests on rough horizontal ground. A rope attached to the box makes an angle of 20° above the horizontal. When the tension in the rope is 30 N, the box is on the point of moving. Find the coefficient of friction between the box and the ground. (g = 10 m s⁻²)

Two horizontal forces act on a particle: 8 N along the positive x-axis, and 5 N at an angle of 60° to the positive x-axis (anticlockwise). Find the magnitude of the resultant force and the angle it makes with the positive x-axis.
scheme: M1: resolve both forces in the x- and y-directions

long.q: A particle of mass 4 kg rests on a rough plane inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where sin α = 0.6. A horizontal force of 50 N, acting in the vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope, pushes the particle towards the plane, and the particle is on the point of moving up the plane. Find the coefficient of friction. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: M1: resolve perpendicular to the plane, including both forces
M1: resolve along the plane with friction acting down the plane

topics.name: Mechanics: Kinematics of motion in a straight line

questions.q: A particle moves with constant acceleration from rest to 12 m s⁻¹ in 4 s. How far does it go?
On a velocity–time graph, the area under the graph gives the…
questions.why: Area = velocity × time = displacement; the gradient is the acceleration.

questions.q: A stone is dropped from rest (g = 10 m s⁻²). What is its speed after 3 s?
A particle has velocity v = 3t² − 2t m s⁻¹. What is its acceleration when t = 2?
questions.why: a = dv/dt = 6t − 2 = 10 m s⁻².

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upwards at 15 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is its greatest height above the point of projection?
questions.why: At the top v = 0: 0 = 15² − 2 × 10 × s, so s = 225/20 = 11.25 m. Omitting the factor 2 gives 22.5 m.

long.q: The diagram shows the velocity–time graph of a cyclist, who accelerates from rest to 12 m s⁻¹ in 4 s, rides at that speed for 6 s, then decelerates uniformly to rest in 3 s. Find the total distance travelled and the deceleration.
scheme: M1: distance = area under the graph

long.q: A stone is thrown vertically upwards with speed 15 m s⁻¹ from a point 20 m above the ground. Find its greatest height above the ground, and the time it takes to reach the ground. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: A1: 11.25 m above the point, so 31.25 m above the ground

long.q: A particle moves in a straight line, starting from rest at O. Its velocity t seconds later is v = 12t − 3t² m s⁻¹, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5. Find (a) its acceleration when t = 1, (b) its greatest velocity, (c) the total distance it travels in the 5 seconds.
scheme: B1: greatest velocity when a = 0, t = 2: 12 m s⁻¹
B1: v = 0 at t = 4, so the particle turns back

long.q: Car A starts from rest at a set of traffic lights and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻². At the same instant car B passes the lights travelling at a constant 14 m s⁻¹ in the same direction. Find the time at which A overtakes B, and A's speed at that moment.
scheme: M1: displacements t² for A and 14t for B
A1: speed of A = 28 m s⁻¹

long.q: A particle moving with constant acceleration passes a point A with speed 4 m s⁻¹, and 8 seconds later passes a point B with speed 20 m s⁻¹. Find the acceleration, the distance AB, and the speed of the particle at the midpoint of AB.

questions.q: What is the momentum of a 2 kg particle moving at 3 m s⁻¹?
questions.why: Momentum = mv = 2 × 3 = 6 N s.

questions.q: A 3 kg particle moving at 4 m s⁻¹ hits a 1 kg particle at rest and they coalesce. Their common speed is…
questions.why: Momentum is conserved: 3 × 4 = 4v, so v = 3 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: In a collision with no external impulse, which is always conserved?
questions.why: Total momentum is conserved; kinetic energy usually isn't (some is lost).

questions.q: Particle A (2 kg) moving at 5 m s⁻¹ meets particle B (3 kg) moving towards it at 2 m s⁻¹. After the collision A moves back at 1 m s⁻¹. What is B's velocity after the collision?
o: 6 m s⁻¹ in A's original direction
2/3 m s⁻¹ in A's original direction
2 m s⁻¹ in A's original direction
2 m s⁻¹ in B's original direction
questions.why: Taking A's direction as positive: 2(5) + 3(−2) = 2(−1) + 3v, so 4 = −2 + 3v and v = 2 m s⁻¹, in A's original direction.

questions.q: A 2 kg particle moving at 6 m s⁻¹ strikes a 1 kg particle at rest and they coalesce. How much kinetic energy is lost?
questions.why: Common speed = 12/3 = 4 m s⁻¹. KE before = ½ × 2 × 36 = 36 J; after = ½ × 3 × 16 = 24 J; loss = 12 J.

long.q: A particle P of mass 0.3 kg moving at 5 m s⁻¹ collides with a particle Q of mass 0.2 kg moving towards it at 2 m s⁻¹. After the collision, P moves at 1 m s⁻¹ in its original direction. Find the speed and direction of Q after the collision.
scheme: M1: conservation of momentum, with signs for direction
A1: in P's original direction of motion
long.ans: 4 m s⁻¹, in P's original direction

long.q: A particle A of mass 0.4 kg moving at 6 m s⁻¹ collides directly with a particle B of mass 0.2 kg moving towards it. The particles coalesce, and the combined particle moves at 3 m s⁻¹ in A's original direction. (a) Find the speed of B before the collision. (b) If instead B's speed before the collision had been 15 m s⁻¹, find the speed and direction of the combined particle.
scheme: M1: conservation of momentum with opposite signs for A and B
A1: 1 m s⁻¹ in B's original direction
long.ans: 3 m s⁻¹; 1 m s⁻¹ in B's original direction

long.q: Three particles A, B and C, of masses 0.5 kg, 0.3 kg and 0.2 kg, lie in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface, with B between A and C. A is projected towards B with speed 4 m s⁻¹; after the collision A moves on at 1 m s⁻¹ in the same direction. B then collides with C, which is at rest, and they coalesce. Find the speed of B after the first collision and the speed of the combined particle, and explain whether A collides again.
scheme: M1: momentum for the first collision
M1: momentum for the second collision: 0.3 × 5 = 0.5V
B1: no further collision, because A (1 m s⁻¹) is slower than the combined particle (3 m s⁻¹) ahead of it

long.q: A particle P of mass 0.25 kg moving at 8 m s⁻¹ collides directly with a particle Q moving in the opposite direction at 3 m s⁻¹. After the collision P moves back at 2 m s⁻¹ and Q moves at 2 m s⁻¹ in P's original direction. Find the mass of Q.
scheme: M1: conservation of momentum with consistent signs

long.q: A sphere of mass 4 kg moving at u m s⁻¹ collides directly with a sphere of mass 1 kg at rest. After the collision both move in the original direction; the 1 kg sphere moves at 6 m s⁻¹, which is twice the speed of the 4 kg sphere. Find u and the loss of kinetic energy in the collision.
scheme: B1: speed of the 4 kg sphere after = 3 m s⁻¹
M1: KE before − KE after = ½ × 4 × 4.5² − (½ × 4 × 3² + ½ × 1 × 6²)

questions.q: A 5 kg box on a smooth floor is pulled by a 20 N horizontal force. What is its acceleration?
Two particles hang on either side of a smooth, light pulley on a light string. The tension is…
questions.why: A light string over a smooth pulley has the same tension throughout.

questions.q: A 60 kg person stands in a lift accelerating upwards at 2 m s⁻² (g = 10 m s⁻²). The floor pushes up with…
A 4 kg block slides down a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is its acceleration?
questions.why: The only force along the plane is the weight component mg sin 30°, so a = g sin 30° = 5 m s⁻², whatever the mass.

questions.q: A 3 kg block on a smooth horizontal table is joined by a light string over a smooth pulley at the edge to a 2 kg particle hanging freely. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the acceleration of the system?
questions.why: The only unbalanced force on the system is the hanging weight 20 N, acting on a total mass of 5 kg, so a = 20/5 = 4 m s⁻².

long.q: Particles A of mass 3 kg and B of mass 2 kg are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string that passes over a smooth fixed pulley. They are released from rest with the string taut. Find the acceleration of the particles and the tension in the string. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: M1: Newton's second law for each particle

long.q: A lift of mass 500 kg carries a man of mass 70 kg. The lift is pulled upwards by a cable and accelerates upwards at 0.5 m s⁻². Find the tension in the cable and the force exerted on the man by the floor of the lift. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: M1: Newton's second law for the lift and man together
M1: Newton's second law for the man alone

long.q: A particle is released from rest on a rough plane inclined at 25° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.3. Find the acceleration of the particle and its speed after it has moved 2 m down the plane. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: M1: Newton's second law along the plane: mg sin 25° − 0.3mg cos 25° = ma

long.q: A block A of mass 4 kg lies on a rough horizontal table, where the coefficient of friction is 0.25. A light inextensible string attached to A passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table and carries a particle B of mass 2 kg hanging freely. The system is released from rest. (a) Find the acceleration and the tension in the string. (b) B hits the floor after falling 0.75 m and does not rebound. Find the speed of B as it hits the floor and the further distance A travels before coming to rest (A does not reach the pulley). (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: M1: Newton's second law for A and B (or the whole system): 20 − 10 = 6a
M1: after B lands, A decelerates at μg = 2.5 m s⁻²

long.q: A car of mass 1200 kg tows a trailer of mass 400 kg along a horizontal road using a light rigid towbar. The resistances to motion are 500 N on the car and 100 N on the trailer, and the car's driving force is 2000 N. (a) Find the acceleration and the tension in the towbar. (b) The driving force is removed, with the resistances unchanged. Find the magnitude of the force in the towbar and state whether it is a tension or a thrust.
scheme: M1: new deceleration 600/1600 = 0.375 m s⁻², applied to the trailer
long.ans: 0.875 m s⁻², 450 N; thrust of 50 N

questions.q: A 10 N force moves its point of application 3 m in its own direction. The work done is…
questions.why: Work = force × distance in the direction of the force = 30 J.

questions.q: A car moves at 20 m s⁻¹ with a driving force of 500 N. Its power is…
What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg particle moving at 5 m s⁻¹?
questions.why: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 25 = 25 J.

questions.q: A 0.5 kg particle is released from rest and falls 20 m with no air resistance. Using energy, what is its speed at the bottom? (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.why: Loss of PE = gain of KE: mgh = ½mv², so v² = 2gh = 400 and v = 20 m s⁻¹; the mass cancels.

questions.q: An 800 kg car moves at a constant 15 m s⁻¹ up a slope inclined at α to the horizontal, where sin α = 0.1, against a resistance of 400 N. What is the power of the engine? (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.why: At constant speed the driving force = 400 + 800 × 10 × 0.1 = 1200 N, so P = Fv = 1200 × 15 = 18 000 W = 18 kW.

long.q: A car of mass 1200 kg moves on a horizontal road against a constant resistance of 600 N. Its engine works at 30 kW. Find the acceleration of the car when its speed is 20 m s⁻¹.
scheme: M1: driving force = P ÷ v = 1500 N

long.q: A block of mass 5 kg is projected with speed 8 m s⁻¹ up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.2. Use an energy method to find the distance the block travels up the plane before coming to rest. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: M1: KE lost = PE gained + work done against friction

long.q: A car of mass 1000 kg has a maximum power of 40 kW. It travels up a straight hill inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where sin α = 0.05, against a constant resistance of 800 N. Find the maximum speed of the car up the hill. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: M1: at maximum speed, driving force = resistance + weight component = 800 + 1000 × 10 × 0.05

long.q: A crate of mass 30 kg is pulled at constant speed for 12 m along a rough horizontal floor by a rope inclined at 15° above the horizontal. The tension in the rope is 100 N. Find the work done by the tension, and the coefficient of friction between the crate and the floor. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: B1: speed is constant, so work done against friction is also 1160 J (friction = 96.6 N)

long.q: A cyclist and her bicycle have a total mass of 80 kg. She freewheels from rest down a straight hill 400 m long, with a vertical drop of 20 m, and reaches a speed of 12 m s⁻¹ at the bottom. Find the work done against resistance, and the average resistance force. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
scheme: B1: gain of KE = ½ × 80 × 12² = 5760 J
M1: work against resistance = PE loss − KE gain

questions.q: What is the median of 3, 7, 7, 9, 12, 15?
questions.why: Six values: the median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th, (7 + 9) ÷ 2 = 8.

questions.q: In a histogram, the area of each bar is proportional to the…
questions.why: Height is frequency density, so area = density × width = frequency.

questions.q: n = 10, Σx = 60 and Σx² = 400. What is the variance?
questions.why: Mean = 6; variance = Σx²/n − mean² = 40 − 36 = 4.

questions.q: A box plot has lower quartile 12 and upper quartile 20. Using 1.5 × IQR beyond a quartile, which value is an outlier?
questions.why: IQR = 8, so the limit is 20 + 12 = 32: only 33 is beyond it.

questions.q: Which average is least affected by extreme outliers in a skewed data distribution?
questions.why: The median depends only on rank order and position, making it resistant to extreme outliers, unlike the mean.

long.q: The times, in minutes, taken by 8 students to finish a puzzle are 12, 15, 9, 20, 14, 11, 16, 23. Find the mean and the standard deviation.
In a histogram, the class 10 ≤ x < 15 has frequency 30 and the class 15 ≤ x < 25 has frequency 40. Find the frequency density of each class.

The table summarises the times, t minutes, that 50 people spent in a shop: 0 ≤ t < 10: 5 people; 10 ≤ t < 20: 12; 20 ≤ t < 30: 18; 30 ≤ t < 50: 15. Calculate estimates of the mean and the standard deviation of the times.
scheme: M1: variance = Σfx²/Σf − mean², with Σfx² = 38 075

long.q: For 20 values of x, Σ(x − 50) = 84 and Σ(x − 50)² = 1250. Find the mean and the standard deviation of x, and the value of Σx².

The marks of 15 students in a test, in order, are 3, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 24, 41. (a) Find the median and the quartiles. (b) An outlier is a value more than 1.5 × the interquartile range above the upper quartile or below the lower quartile. Identify any outliers. (c) Give one reason why the median is a better average than the mean for these data.
scheme: B1: lower quartile 10 and upper quartile 19
B1: the median is not affected by the extreme value 41, which pulls the mean upwards
long.ans: median 14, quartiles 10 and 19; 41 is an outlier

questions.q: In how many ways can 5 different books be arranged on a shelf?
questions.why: Five choices for the first place, then four, three, two, one: 5! = 120.

questions.q: In how many ways can 3 people be chosen from 8?
questions.why: The order doesn't matter: ⁸C₃ = 56.

questions.q: How many different arrangements are there of the letters of LEVEL?
questions.why: 5! ÷ (2! × 2!) for the repeated L and E = 30.

questions.q: Six people sit in a row. Two of them must sit together. How many arrangements?
questions.why: Treat the pair as one: 5! ways, × 2 for the pair's order = 240.

questions.q: A team of 5 is chosen from 7 boys and 4 girls. How many teams contain exactly 2 girls?
questions.why: Choose 2 of the 4 girls and 3 of the 7 boys: ⁴C₂ × ⁷C₃ = 6 × 35 = 210.

long.q: Find the number of different arrangements of the letters of the word PARALLEL. How many of these begin and end with L?
scheme: M1: fix an L at each end; arrange the other 6 with A repeated: 6! ÷ 2!

long.q: A committee of 4 is chosen from 6 men and 5 women. How many different committees contain at least one woman?
scheme: M1: subtract the all-men committees ⁶C₄ = 15

long.q: Seven people, including Ali and Bea, sit in a row of seven seats. Find the number of different arrangements in which (a) Ali and Bea sit next to each other, (b) Ali and Bea do not sit next to each other.
scheme: M1: treat Ali and Bea as one unit: 6! × 2

long.q: A team of 5 is chosen from 4 forwards, 6 midfielders and 3 defenders. Find the number of different teams that contain exactly 2 midfielders and at least 1 defender.
scheme: B1: ⁶C₂ = 15 ways to choose the midfielders
M1: other 3 from the 7 forwards and defenders with at least one defender: ⁷C₃ − ⁴C₃ (or add the cases 18 + 12 + 1)

long.q: Four-digit numbers are formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8, with no digit repeated. Find how many of these numbers are greater than 5000, and how many are both greater than 5000 and even.
scheme: M1: first digit 5, 6 or 8, then 5 × 4 × 3 for the rest
M1: split by first digit and count the even last digits remaining
A1: first digit 5: 36; first digit 6 or 8: 24 each

questions.q: Events A and B are independent when…
o: A and B can't both happen
questions.why: Mutually exclusive events are a different idea (P(A ∩ B) = 0).

questions.q: P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.7. What is P(A ∩ B)?
P(A | B) is…
questions.why: Given B, only the part of A inside B counts, out of all of B.

questions.q: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the total is 7?

questions.q: If events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.4, what is P(A ∩ B)?
questions.why: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur simultaneously, so their intersection probability P(A ∩ B) is identically 0.

long.q: A bag contains 3 red counters and 2 blue counters. Two counters are taken at random, without replacement, as shown in the tree diagram. Find the probability that (a) both are red, (b) they are different colours, (c) the first is red, given that they are different colours.
scheme: M1: P(first red and different) ÷ P(different)

long.q: Events A and B have P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.65. Determine whether A and B are independent.
scheme: A1: P(A) × P(B) = 0.15 as well, so independent

long.q: 4% of a population have a certain condition. A test gives a positive result for 95% of people who have the condition and for 10% of people who do not. A person is chosen at random and tested. Find the probability that the result is positive, and the probability that the person has the condition given that the result is positive.
scheme: M1: P(condition | positive) = P(condition and positive) ÷ P(positive)

long.q: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown. Event A is 'the total is 7' and event B is 'at least one die shows a 6'. Find P(A), P(B) and P(A ∩ B). Determine whether A and B are independent, and whether they are mutually exclusive.
scheme: M1: compare P(A) × P(B) = 11/216 with P(A ∩ B) = 12/216
A1: not independent; not mutually exclusive, since P(A ∩ B) ≠ 0

long.q: Ali and Ben take turns to throw a fair six-sided die, Ali throwing first. The first person to throw a 6 wins. Find the probability that Ali wins on his second throw, and the probability that Ali wins.
scheme: M1: three throws: two non-sixes then a six
M1: sum of a geometric series with ratio 25/36

scheme: M1: correct method for one probability, e.g. P(X = 0) = ⁴C₃/⁶C₃

long.q: A biased coin shows heads with probability 0.3. It is thrown repeatedly until it shows a head; X is the number of throws needed, including the head. Find P(X = 4), P(X > 3) and E(X).
scheme: M1: P(X > 3) = P(first three are tails) = 0.7³

long.q: The random variable X has a binomial distribution with E(X) = 6 and Var(X) = 4.2. Find the parameters of the distribution and P(X = 5).

30% of the people in a large town own a bicycle. A random sample of 80 people is taken. Use a suitable approximation to find the probability that more than 30 of them own a bicycle, and justify your use of the approximation.

long.q: The lengths of metal rods are normally distributed with mean 25 cm. 15% of the rods are longer than 28 cm. Find the standard deviation of the lengths, and the expected number of rods shorter than 23 cm in a batch of 200.

The times taken by runners to complete a fun run are normally distributed with mean 42 minutes and standard deviation 6 minutes. (a) Find the time below which 90% of the runners finish. (b) Three runners are chosen at random. Find the probability that all three finish in less than 45 minutes.

questions.why: For a Poisson distribution, mean = variance = λ.

questions.q: A Type I error is…
questions.why: Its probability equals the significance level (for continuous tests).

questions.q: X ~ Po(2) and Y ~ Po(3) are independent. What is the distribution of X + Y?
questions.why: The sum of independent Poisson variables is Poisson with the means added.

questions.q: X ~ N(20, 9) and Y ~ N(15, 16) are independent. What is Var(X − Y)?
questions.why: For independent variables variances add even when subtracting: Var(X − Y) = 9 + 16 = 25.

questions.q: A continuous random variable has pdf f(x) = kx² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3, and 0 otherwise. What is k?
questions.why: The total probability is 1: ∫₀³ kx² dx = k × 27/3 = 9k = 1, so k = 1/9.

long.q: The number of emails a shop receives per hour has a Poisson distribution with mean 3.2. Find the probability that it receives exactly 2 emails in a given hour, and at least 1 email in a 30-minute period.
A machine fills bags whose masses are normally distributed with standard deviation 4 g. A random sample of 25 bags has mean 498.2 g. Test at the 5% level whether the mean mass is less than 500 g.
scheme: A1: reject H₀: evidence the mean is less than 500 g

long.q: The continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) = k(4x − x²) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3, and f(x) = 0 otherwise. Find the value of k, E(X), and P(X < 1).
